pharm: Reversible CXCR4 chemokine-receptor antagonist that blocks SDF-1alpha (CXCL12) binding, mobilizing CD34+ hematopoietic stem cells from the marrow into peripheral blood for apheresis.
quick: 0.24 mg/kg SC (actual body weight) ~11 h before apheresis; max 40 mg/day
Can cause fetal harm; use effective contraception
Not recommended during and for 1 week after the final dose
CBC/platelets, white cell count, spleen size/pain
summary: Plerixafor is a CXCR4 antagonist used in combination with G-CSF (filgrastim) to mobilize CD34+ hematopoietic stem cells into the peripheral blood for collection and autologous transplantation in non-Hodgkin lymphoma and multiple myeloma. It is given subcutaneously about 11 hours before apheresis after 4 days of G-CSF. Key warnings include hypersensitivity/anaphylactic reactions, splenic enlargement/rupture, thrombocytopenia, leukocytosis, and embryo-fetal toxicity. It is not indicated for leukemia (risk of mobilizing leukemic cells).
indications: In combination with G-CSF (filgrastim) to mobilize hematopoietic stem cells to the peripheral blood for collection and autologous transplantation in patients with non-Hodgkin lymphoma
In combination with G-CSF to mobilize hematopoietic stem cells for autologous transplantation in patients with multiple myeloma

dosage.t: ~11 hours before apheresis, after 4 days of once-daily G-CSF
dosage.n: May repeat for up to 4 consecutive days; dosing validated to 175% of ideal body weight

admin: Administer by subcutaneous injection from a single-dose, preservative-free vial
Give approximately 11 hours before initiation of each apheresis, following 4 days of once-daily G-CSF
Inspect for particulate matter and discoloration before use
Observe the patient for at least 30 minutes after the first dose for hypersensitivity reactions
Have measures for anaphylaxis available during administration
moa: Plerixafor reversibly antagonizes the CXCR4 chemokine receptor, blocking binding of its ligand SDF-1alpha (CXCL12). This disrupts the anchoring of CD34+ hematopoietic stem cells in the bone marrow, releasing them into the peripheral circulation where they can be collected by apheresis.

relative: Leukemia (not indicated; risk of mobilizing leukemic cells into the apheresis product)
monitor: Spleen size and left upper quadrant/shoulder pain

preg: Can cause fetal harm (embryo-fetal mortality and malformations in animals). Advise effective contraception during therapy and for 1 week after the final dose.
lact: Breastfeeding is not recommended during treatment and for 1 week after the final dose.
renal: For patients with CrCl 50 mL/min or less, reduce the dose by about one-third to 0.16 mg/kg (maximum 27 mg/day). Plerixafor is predominantly eliminated unchanged by the kidneys.
hepatic: No specific dose adjustment; plerixafor is not metabolized and is eliminated predominantly by the renal route.

major: No clinically significant CYP-mediated interactions (not metabolized by CYP450)
moderate: Drugs that reduce renal function or compete for renal tubular secretion may increase plerixafor exposure
minor: Not a substrate or inhibitor of P-glycoprotein
interactions.diagnostics: Expect predictable transient leukocytosis and mild thrombocytopenia on laboratory monitoring.

serious: Splenic enlargement and risk of rupture
rare: Potential mobilization of tumor cells into the apheresis product
emergency: Splenic rupture (left upper quadrant or shoulder-tip pain)

monitoring: White blood cell count / complete blood count
Spleen size and symptoms (left upper quadrant or scapular/shoulder pain)
Signs of hypersensitivity during and for 30 minutes after dosing
counsel: Report any signs of allergic reaction such as hives, rash, shortness of breath, or faintness
Report pain in the left upper abdomen or at the tip of the shoulder (possible spleen problem)
You may feel lightheaded or faint after the injection - tell your care team
Common effects include diarrhea, nausea, tiredness, and injection-site reactions
Use effective contraception during treatment and for 1 week afterward; do not breastfeed during this time
pk: Peak plasma ~30-60 min; peak CD34+ cells with G-CSF at 10-14 h (basis for ~11 h timing)
Mobilizing effect over ~10-14 hours after a dose
pearls: Always used together with 4 days of G-CSF (filgrastim), not as monotherapy
Timing matters - give ~11 hours before apheresis so peak CD34+ mobilization aligns with collection
Reduce the dose to 0.16 mg/kg when CrCl is 50 mL/min or below
Not for leukemia - it can mobilize leukemic cells into the apheresis product
Expect predictable transient leukocytosis and mild thrombocytopenia
missed: Timing relative to apheresis is critical and is managed by the transplant team; there is no patient self-administered make-up dose. A missed or mistimed dose is addressed by the apheresis schedule.
overdose: Doses above 0.24 mg/kg are associated with more gastrointestinal upset and vasovagal/orthostatic hypotension and syncope. There is no specific antidote; management is supportive with monitoring of blood pressure and cardiac status.
